subject: scores from out of sample data

messages.author: 30719b75cbb1994e
messages.subject: scores from out of sample data
parts:
Let's suppose that I estimated IRT parameters with a sample data (i.e. training sample) and perhaps a another sample covdata (for formulas in mirt and/or fixed in mixedmirt). My question is:
- Is there an easy way to estimate fscores (i.e. thetas) from another sample data that is independent of the sample used to estimate the model parameters (i.e. testing sample). Correspondingly, if I use mixef and/or fixed in the case of scores for mixedmirt, can I also use the covdata information of that independent sample to get the theta scores?
I played around and modified the @Data info in the mod output and it seems to work for fscores. I just wonder if there is an easiest way to achieve estimated scores from an independent sample.
- Also, how can I change the scale for the thetas from the typical range [-6 6] to reflect let's say that the theta scores are samples from a normal distribution with a given mean mu and standard deviation s.
Thanks in advance,

parts: On Wed, Jun 2, 2021 at 5:41 PM Felix Carbonell <felixm...@gmail.com> wrote:

Let's suppose that I estimated IRT parameters with a sample data (i.e. training sample) and perhaps a another sample covdata (for formulas in mirt and/or fixed in mixedmirt). My question is:
- Is there an easy way to estimate fscores (i.e. thetas) from another sample data that is independent of the sample used to estimate the model parameters (i.e. testing sample). Correspondingly, if I use mixef and/or fixed in the case of scores for mixedmirt, can I also use the covdata information of that independent sample to get the theta scores?
I played around and modified the @Data info in the mod output and it seems to work for fscores. I just wonder if there is an easiest way to achieve estimated scores from an independent sample.

It's trickier to do this, and you're right the package doesn't provide easy support of the this out-of-the-box. What you could do is first estimate you calibration model to obtain the parameter estimates, and supply these as fixed values to a similarly 'estimated' model using the testing dataset (converging instantly as all parameters would be fixed). From there, the new dataset would be properly stored internally, and so you could obtain the factor scores/random effects by way of this dummy model.

- Also, how can I change the scale for the thetas from the typical range [-6 6] to reflect let's say that the theta scores are samples from a normal distribution with a given mean mu and standard deviation s.

You can either do this in the model specification component by a) changing the mean/variance combinations (note: if you use the EM algorithm be sure to adjust the range of the numerical quadrature accordingly), though I don't recommend this as it can lead to numerical problems, or b) just change the scale yourself post-estimation as the metric is generally arbitrary anyway. HTH.

Phil
 
Thanks in advance,
